key_insight: A dense array of flexible asymmetric leaflets in an oscillatory confined flow can collectively rectify motion and generate net transport, with an optimal elastoviscous balance maximizing pumping.
engineering_relevance: The results provide a design rule for passive microfluidic transport and bioinspired flow-control devices where geometry, density, and leaflet stiffness must be tuned together.
method: Numerical study of multiple interacting leaflets in a low-Re channel
Symmetrically oscillating plates used to remove background pressure-driven asymmetry
Analytical steady-limit framework extended to time-dependent channel oscillations
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the authors compare transport across leaflet densities and elastoviscous numbers, identifying configurations that maximize net flow.
watch_item: The framework is developed for low-Re oscillatory conditions in a confined idealized geometry, so performance may differ under real-world unsteady, inertial, or fabrication-limited conditions.
paper_title: On the rectification of oscillatory flows by flexible leaflets in a confined geometry
